source_version: Capella (continuously deployed, no discrete version number)

concepts.label: URL binding
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a Binding sub-type (alongside Bucket bindings) that maps an alias to an external URL plus an authentication mode (here 'No Auth'), which the `curl()` built-in uses as its first-argument target instead of a raw URL string

concepts.label: curl() built-in function
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the built-in JavaScript function (`curl(method, urlBindingAlias, requestObj)`) that performs an outbound HTTP request from inside a handler or Timer callback, returning a response object with `.status` and `.body`

concepts.label: No Auth (URL binding authentication mode)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - one setting value of the URL binding's Authentication field; other modes are implied but not documented on this page

relations.subject: eventing:curl-function
relations.evidence:
// Performs the cURL request using the URL alias form the settings  
        var response = curl('GET', exchangeRateApi, request);

relations.subject: eventing:recurring-timer-pattern
relations.evidence: The Timer callback function creates the initial Timer 30 seconds into the future. It then creates the next Timer 2-N at the start of the following day.

relations.subject: eventing:curl-function
relations.evidence: You must use a real IP address if you're not on the Couchbase Server.

notable_absence.finding: The prerequisite section offers a self-hosted Python HTTP server as a fallback if the public `frankfurter.app` exchange-rate API is offline, and shows curl-testing that fallback on `localhost:8001` - but the actual Function example is only ever shown wired to the public API via the `exchangeRateApi` URL binding; the fallback path's own binding configuration is not documented, only implied.

cross_product_finding: This is the first page in the batch to document a Binding type other than Bucket (URL binding with an Authentication mode setting), and the first to show a handler making outbound calls to a resource entirely outside Couchbase (a public third-party REST API) rather than reading/writing Couchbase keyspaces - a genuinely distinct integration surface from the KV/SQL++-centric examples on every other page in this batch.
